edges.description: Loss of mitochondrial inorganic pyrophosphatase catalytic activity and temperature-induced inactivation of residual mutant PPA2 prevent clearance of intramitochondrial inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi), causing PPi buildup within the mitochondrial matrix.

Unresolved intramitochondrial PPi accumulation inactivates the mitochondrial energy-transducing system and prevents maintenance of a sufficient electrical potential across the inner mitochondrial membrane.

Collapse of the inner mitochondrial membrane potential and loss of functional mitochondria impair oxidative phosphorylation (including cardiac complex I and IV activities) and precipitate cellular ATP depletion.

edges.description: Necrotic loss of energy-depleted cardiomyocytes triggers cardiac fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix deposition, producing focal and mid-myocardial replacement fibrosis.
Loss of functional cardiomyocytes and myofibrillar disarray directly reduce ventricular systolic force generation.
Focal and mid-myocardial collagen deposition manifests clinically and radiologically as myocardial fibrosis on late gadolinium enhancement cardiac MRI and autopsy histology.

Patchy mid-myocardial fibrosis creates conduction heterogeneity and re-entrant circuits that, together with acute bioenergetic crisis, trigger malignant ventricular tachyarrhythmias and sudden cardiac arrest.
Extensive mid-myocardial replacement fibrosis stiffens and weakens the ventricular walls, contributing to dilated cardiomyopathy, acute heart failure, and cardiogenic shock.
Electrical instability in the fibrotic, energy-depleted myocardium degenerates into lethal ventricular fibrillation.
Myocardial electrical instability manifests as pulseless or sustained ventricular tachycardia.
Malignant ventricular arrhythmias and pulseless electrical activity cause abrupt cessation of effective cardiac mechanical output.
Refractory ventricular fibrillation, pulseless ventricular tachycardia, or asystole/PEA frequently resists resuscitation and results in sudden cardiac death.
Impaired myocardial contractility and myocyte loss manifest structurally as left ventricular or biventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction on echocardiography.
Severe ventricular systolic failure leads to acute or rapidly progressive heart failure.
Fulminant pump failure in infants and young children produces acute cardiogenic shock and multiorgan failure.
Fever/hyperthermia during viral infection further reduces the residual catalytic activity of temperature-sensitive mutant PPA2 enzymes.

ACSS1-mediated esterification of ethanol-derived acetic acid generates an acute intramitochondrial PPi surge that cannot be hydrolyzed by deficient PPA2, directly exacerbating mitochondrial matrix PPi accumulation.

nodes.description: Biallelic hypomorphic missense variants or compound heterozygous missense/truncating variants in PPA2 severely reduce mitochondrial inorganic pyrophosphatase activity in the mitochondrial matrix. Because PPA2 catalyzes the hydrolysis of inorganic pyrophosphate (PPi) into two orthophosphate ions, reduced PPA2 activity impairs PPi clearance during high-flux mitochondrial biosynthetic reactions (DNA, RNA, protein, and lipid synthesis) and short-chain fatty-acid/acetate activation. Residual enzymatic activity of recombinant mutant PPA2 proteins correlates with age at onset and clinical severity: variants associated with neonatal or early infantile lethality (such as p.Pro167Leu and p.Glu172Lys) retain only 5%–10% wild-type activity, whereas variants permissive for survival into adolescence (such as p.Pro228Leu) retain 24%–28% activity. Furthermore, missense PPA2 variants exhibit temperature sensitivity in vitro, so febrile viral illnesses or modest ethanol/acetic acid loads acutely overwhelm residual PPi hydrolysis capacity.
